answer: An AI-agent economy can curb Sybil attacks using continuous proof-of-work. To participate, each agent must periodically solve a cipher challenge seeded by an unpredictable yarrow entropy pool. This imposes an unavoidable, verifiable cost of hardware cycles and electricity for every identity an attacker sustains. While this avoids relying on a centralized identity bridge, it inherently penalizes compute-constrained agents and introduces transaction latency.
